data.narrative:
Living Carbon, a Series A biotech company founded by Maddie Hall and Patrick Mellor, has raised $36M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of three triangulation methods considered, only stage-progression analysis is applicable. This method uses the $36M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage step-ups, yielding a $72M implied valuation. Peer-median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-stage and valuation-tier comparables within the biotech sector (fewer than 3 datapoints after filtering). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple—the Biotech & Health median stands at 6.2x across three public tickers—cannot be deployed without revenue disclosure, which private companies rarely provide.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $61M (low, representing a 1.7x step-up) to $83M (high, representing a 2.3x step-up), with a median of $72M. The primary uncertainty stems from reliance on a single applicable method. Revenue visibility and concrete peer transaction data at the Series A stage would strengthen conviction in this range.
